What's new

What changed, release by release.

Every change to VertexForm that you can see or hear, newest first. It's the project's changelog, so nothing here is planned work: all of it is live.

2.15.024 November 2026

A side rail that stays out of the way

  • On a wide screen the section rail now rests as a thin strip of ticks at the left edge, giving the page its width back. Point at it and it slides open with the section names; it also pops out for a moment when you reach a new section, so you can see where you are.

Motion on proper curves

  • Every animation in the site and the trainer now moves on a named easing curve (cubic-out for things arriving, quart-out for settling, back-out for pops, in-out cubic for travel), so motion starts, slows and lands the same way everywhere.
2.14.123 November 2026

A cleaner opening

  • The opening now starts the moment the page appears: a grid powers on and crosshairs draw out while the points arrive. When all 33 lock, viewfinder brackets snap round the figure, and as the page opens the figure glides straight into its place on the page instead of starting over.
2.14.023 November 2026

A new opening

  • The first visit now opens in 3D: the 33 tracking points fly in from all around the room and lock onto a figure that turns to face you, while the VertexForm wordmark rises behind it and fills in once tracking locks. Then the figure rushes toward you and the screen splits open onto the page.

New ways into each section

  • Moving between sections on a wide screen now reveals the next one over the last, each in its own way: a protractor sweeping round with its angle shown, a calibration scan passing down, a portal opening out of the figure, ruler slats opening, and the horizon opening from the middle.
2.13.023 November 2026

Scenes that turn

  • On a wide screen, every part of the homepage is now one full screen: you never scroll down inside a section to read it. Each one holds still while you read, then the page turns to the next in 3D: like a cube turning, a door swinging open, a page flipping down and up. From the top, the camera dives into the figure while the figure swings round.
  • Stop between two sections and the page glides to the nearer one.
  • The story and skill paths open on a title card that zooms out as you go on.

Calmer ink

  • The ink behind the page is fainter and thinner, clears faster and changes colour slowly, so it stays out of the way of the text.
2.12.022 November 2026

A tree in flower

  • In the 3D skill tree, every skill now grows on its own stem out of the branches instead of sitting inside them. Unlocked skills carry a spray of flowers and buds, the next skill is a bud just starting to open, and locked ones are dormant buds on a bare twig. Branches between two unlocked skills flower along their length.

Words that move

  • Homepage headings rise in letter by letter, each section's opening paragraph lights up word by word as you reach it, and the section labels spell themselves in.
2.11.020 November 2026

The skill tree grows in 3D

  • On a wide screen, each skill path is now a real tree in 3D. The trunk and branches grow up from the ground tier by tier, unlocked skills open into flowers, the next one is an amber bud, and leaves come in along the branches you've earned.
  • Every skill carries a label with the workout that trains it, like "Push-up × 15 · avg 90+", and its status. The names rise in letter by letter as the tree grows.
  • The tree turns slowly on its own. Drag to turn it; pick a skill and it swings to the front and lights its branches down to the trunk.
2.10.120 November 2026

Cards that catch the light

  • In the trainer's ring of exercises, a card catches a glint as it turns to the front and when you point at it, and a glint runs round the whole ring once the cards have flown in.
2.10.018 November 2026

The homepage scrolls in

  • On a wide screen, scrolling now moves you forward through the page instead of down it. Each section fills the screen; between them the page holds still while the one you're leaving flies past you and the next one rises out of the distance. From the top, the camera dives into the figure.
2.9.018 November 2026

The trainer's exercises on a ring

  • On a wide screen, the trainer's exercise picker is now a ring of all eighteen cards standing around the live figure. It turns slowly on its own; scroll, drag, the arrow buttons or the arrow keys turn it, and the card at the front is the one on the stage. Click a card (or press Enter) to train it.
2.8.018 November 2026

Ink you can stir

  • The background is ink in water now, not one colour: moving your pointer pours ink in greens, teals, blues and ambers and swirls it, scrolling stirs it, and drops fall in on their own now and then. The smoke behind it shifts between teal, blue and green and leans away from your pointer.

A ring of exercises

  • On a wide screen, all eighteen exercises stand as cards on a ring around the section's heading. Scrolling turns it, it also turns slowly on its own, and clicking a card opens that exercise.

A stronger opening

  • The first visit's calibration now has the 33 points fly in from all over the screen and lock onto the body, a big counter, and the screen splitting open along the horizon onto the page.
2.7.018 November 2026

The rest of the page

  • Every section now opens like the first screen: its number and name, a line that draws across as you scroll to it, and a count from the section itself, like "18 exercises" or "4 steps".
  • Section headings are bigger and set in two weights.
  • The drawings of each exercise, the setup figure and the Form Lab figure glow in their own colours, like the figure at the top.
  • "How it works" walks through its four steps with the same figure drawn in light.
2.6.018 November 2026

The stick figure, drawn in light

  • The figure at the top of the homepage is a stick figure again, now in 3D and made of light: glowing bones, a ring for a head, a bright point on every tracked joint, and faint trails behind the hands and feet, so each rep leaves a trace of its path. The mannequin from 2.5.0 is gone.
  • The same figure squats beside the questions as you scroll and raises its arms at the end of the page.

A new first screen

  • The top of the homepage fills the screen like an instrument: the figure in the middle, a line through it with live readings (the measured angle, the rep, the view angle), an orbit that turns as you drag the view, the exercise as one big word, and the score large in its grade colour.
  • Slow smoke drifts behind the whole page and lights up in the colour of each graded rep.
  • The first visit starts with a short calibration: the 33 points the tracker follows are found one by one, the skeleton is drawn between them, and the screen opens onto the page.

Smoother

  • Start training opens the trainer as a smooth circle with no stutter, and in Chrome the trainer starts loading while your pointer is still on the button.
  • Buttons fill with a circle of colour from the pointer again.
2.5.018 November 2026

A real 3D body

  • The figure in the 3D view at the top of the homepage is now a smooth mannequin with a skeleton, instead of sticks and balls. Every pose comes from the same tracked points the engine scored, so each bend of a knee or elbow is the real one.
  • It arrives as a scan: a band of light passes down the body and leaves it solid, the joint points lighting up as the scan reaches them.
  • Further down, beside the questions, the mannequin does one squat as you scroll: your scroll moves its knees, a tag reads the knee angle, and the view turns around it. At the end of the page it raises its arms beside "Try it on your next set". Wide screens only.

Buttons

  • Buttons scan instead of filling with a circle: a beam sweeps across, the colour follows it, and each letter rolls over as the beam passes.
2.4.117 November 2026

Scrolling

  • Links into the homepage from other pages (the footer's Form Lab, Setup and Questions) now land on their section. Before, they stopped thousands of pixels short, because the story and skill paths grow after the page loads.
  • Scrolling the homepage does less work each frame: the page is measured once when its layout changes instead of by every effect on every frame, and the 3D views no longer re-measure their canvases while they draw.
2.4.03 November 2026

Privacy page

  • A page that says what happens to your camera and your data, in plain words: what's kept in this browser and for how long, what your browser downloads and from where, and how to export or erase everything. The tests check the code keeps its promises: no cookies, no analytics, no uploads.

Finding your way around

  • The footer is a small sitemap: the trainer, the library, the skill paths, how it works, the Form Lab, questions, What's new and privacy.
  • The homepage's exercise list is now a row of small drawings, one per exercise, each opening its page in the library.
  • A missing page says so and offers the homepage, the library and the trainer.
  • Menu links on the homepage stop with the section right under the header, instead of a little way down.

Sharing

  • Links to VertexForm show a preview card with its name and what it does.

Easier to read

  • Hint text is brighter, so it's readable on every background.
  • Pages no longer jump as their fonts load, and nothing scrolls sideways on a phone.
2.3.02 November 2026

Eight more exercises

  • Bulgarian split squat: the front knee and an upright torso, counted only with the back foot up on a bench.
  • Pistol squat: depth on the standing leg, and the free leg has to stay off the floor.
  • Dips: elbows to about 90° on parallel bars.
  • Australian row: chest to a low bar with the body in one straight line.
  • Negative pull-up: graded on how slowly you lower, 3 seconds or more.
  • Pull-up: from a dead hang until the chin clears the bar.
  • L-sit: legs straight and level with the hips, held for time.
  • V-sit: feet raised well above the hips, held for time.
  • Each has its own coaching lines and spoken name in all three voices, so all eighteen exercises can go in a workout.

Skill paths

  • The Legs and Core paths are now tracked from start to finish, and the Pull path up to ten pull-ups.
  • The trainer's menu shows your nearest unlocks: the two skills your saved sets are closest to, what's left in words, and a button to train it.
  • Workouts can plan your next unlocks: one step for each of the skills you're closest to, at its goal amount, so finishing the workout can unlock them.

Exercise library

  • A new page with every exercise: what it scores, what a good rep looks like, the mistakes it flags in the coach's own words, and the skills it unlocks. Each one links straight to its setup in the trainer.

What's new

  • This page: every change you can see or hear, newest first.

A quieter design

  • Lighter headings, solid buttons and ruled figure plates, after comparing the site with Linear, Raycast and Apple. The grade colours now only mean scores.
  • Removed effects that made the site look generated: the light following the pointer, click sparks, magnetic buttons, tilting cards and decoding text.
  • Nothing flashes while the homepage loads, and screens in the trainer grow out of the button you pressed.
2.2.028 October 2026

Exercises and coaching

  • Pike push-up, side plank, hollow hold, mountain climbers and dead hang.
  • Every exercise says its own setup line when you're out of position.
  • Rep replay: watch each rep back beside the ideal form and save the ones you want.
  • Daily challenges for 7, 14 or 30 days.

Skill paths

  • 32 skills in five paths (Push, Pull, Legs, Core, Conditioning), drawn as trees that grow and bloom. Tracked skills unlock from your real saved sets, and each skill shows your best try against its goal.

The website

  • A 3D hero that grades a simulated rep with the real engine, a pinned "How it works" story, exercise popups that turn the drawing into a 3D model, and the Form Lab, where sliders drive the real scoring.
  • The homepage speaks in the trainer's recorded voice.

The trainer

  • The exercise picker is an instrument: the exercise you point at does its rep live.
  • Results land with a grade dial, a rep chart that draws itself and fault dots for every rep they were flagged in.
